title: Open Tree of Life web services

title: Reassessing a cryptic history of early trilobite evolution
note: Primary phylogenetic and palaeobiogeographic reassessment; inferred topology and origin timing remain matrix- and model-conditioned.

title: Burgess Shale fossils illustrate the origin of the mandibulate body plan
note: Primary description and morphology-matrix analysis of Tokummia katalepsis from the Marble Canyon Burgess Shale.

title: Waptia fieldensis Walcott, a mandibulate arthropod from the middle Cambrian Burgess Shale
authors: Vannier, J.; Aria, C.; Taylor, R.S.; Caron, J.-B.
note: Primary redescription based on more than 1,800 Burgess Shale specimens, including figured mandibles and cephalothoracic appendages.

title: An epipodite-bearing crown-group crustacean from the Lower Cambrian
authors: Zhang, X.-G.; Siveter, D.J.; Waloszek, D.; Maas, A.
note: Primary description of phosphatized Yicaris dianensis growth stages and their interpreted eucrustacean position.

title: Phylotranscriptomics to Bring the Understudied into the Fold: Monophyletic Ostracoda, Fossil Placement, and Pancrustacean Phylogeny
authors: Oakley, T.H.; Wolfe, J.M.; Lindgren, A.R.; Zaharoff, A.K.
note: Nine new ostracod 454 transcriptomes were combined with morphology, fossils and other sequence partitions; topology changed across data filters and outgroups.

title: Pancrustacean Evolution Illuminated by Taxon-Rich Genomic-Scale Data Sets with an Expanded Remipede Sampling
authors: Lozano-Fernandez, J.; Giacomelli, M.; Fleming, J.F.; Chen, A.; Vinther, J.; Thomsen, P.F.; Glenner, H.; Palero, F.; Legg, D.A.; Iliffe, T.M.; Pisani, D.; Olesen, J.
note: Taxon-rich phylogenomic study with expanded remipede sampling and explicit sensitivity across analytical approaches.

title: Major Revisions in Pancrustacean Phylogeny and Evidence of Sensitivity to Taxon Sampling
authors: Bernot, J.P.; Owen, C.L.; Wolfe, J.M.; Meland, K.; Olesen, J.; Crandall, K.A.
note: Compares 98- and 105-taxon phylogenomic matrices and demonstrates large topology shifts caused by modest taxon-sampling changes.

title: A new assessment of Rhyniella, the earliest known insect, from the Devonian of Rhynie, Scotland
note: Primary reassessment reporting four head capsules, about ten additional body specimens, an abdomen and a springtail-like furcula.

title: New light shed on the oldest insect
note: Interprets the isolated Rhyniognatha mouthparts as dicondylic insect mandibles with possible pterygote affinity.

title: The presumed oldest flying insect: more likely a myriapod?
note: Three-dimensional reanalysis of NHMUK PI IN 38234 argues that the preserved head structures fit a myriapod, possibly a centipede, better than a flying insect.

title: A molecular palaeobiological exploration of arthropod terrestrialization
authors: Lozano-Fernandez, J.; Carton, R.; Tanner, A.R.; Puttick, M.N.; Blaxter, M.; Vinther, J.; Olesen, J.; Giribet, G.; Edgecombe, G.D.; Pisani, D.
publisher: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
note: Fossil-calibrated analyses of a 57-taxon, 246-gene core dataset compare routes and timing for independent arthropod terrestrializations.

title: Discovery of the oldest known Pterygota in the Lower Carboniferous of the Upper Silesian Basin in the Czech Republic (Insecta: Archaeorthoptera)
authors: Prokop, J.; Nel, A.; Hoch, I.
note: Primary description of a crushed forewing part and counterpart from a lowermost Namurian drill core near Paskov.

title: Knockout of crustacean leg patterning genes suggests that insect wings and body walls evolved from ancient leg segments
note: CRISPR knockout and expression comparisons in Parhyale and insects test serial homology of proximal leg segments, body wall and wings.

title: Phylogenomics resolves the timing and pattern of insect evolution
authors: Misof, B.; Liu, S.; Meusemann, K.; Peters, R.S.; Donath, A.; Frandsen, P.B.; et al.
note: The 1KITE analysis samples 144 insect species and 1,478 protein-coding genes, combines transcriptomic topology with fossil-calibrated time models and archives sequences under BioProject PRJNA183205.

title: The earliest known holometabolous insects
authors: Nel, A.; Roques, P.; Nel, P.; Prokin, A.A.; Bourgoin, T.; Prokop, J.; et al.
note: Describes five Pennsylvanian fossils representing a stem coleopterid, a holometabolous larva, a stem hymenopterid, Hemiptera and Psocodea.

title: A marine stem-myriapod from the Silurian Waukesha Lagerstätte, Wisconsin, USA: terrestrial traits pre-date the transition to land
authors: Briggs, D.E.G.; Lamsdell, J.C.; Kluessendorf, J.; Mikulic, D.G.
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Thirty-five Llandoverian Waukartus specimens preserve uniramous limbs, muscles and endoskeleton; morphology matrices place the taxon on the myriapod stem rather than within crown Myriapoda.
